description: Show one issue, one wiki page or one claim of a PRIVATE project in a public project of the same company — by reference, not as a copy: anybody, signed in or not, can then read that issue (with its comments and files) or that page as it is now, and every later edit; the rest of its project stays closed, and its links to other closed things are counted, never named. A claim is shown with its statement and its status as the register says it — the same status inside and outside — and is cited on the public project's pages by its label. Give exactly one of issueKey, pageId or claimId. Only the owner of the project it belongs to may, and only if they also administer the public project; the public project must be public. Written to both projects' journals. Confirm with the person first: what it shows becomes readable by the whole internet.

claimId.description: The claim to show, by its id (list_claims): its statement and its status, which moves with the register's journal; the journal itself is not shown.

edition.description: For a page: 'current' (default) shows its words as they are now and every later edit; 'approved' shows only its edition in force (approve_wiki_page) — later edits stay unseen until approved, and the page shows nothing while no approval stands. Asking again with the other word switches a page already shown.

pageId.description: The wiki page to show, by its id.

projectKey.description: Key of the public project that will show it, e.g. 'D5'.
